trajectory.patch:
Based on the linker error `undefined reference to '__device_dts_ord_38'`, it is evident that a device driver is not being linked into the final binary. This typically happens when the Kconfig option for the driver is not enabled, or the corresponding devicetree node has `status = "disabled"`.

The error originates from the test `tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction`, which relies on board-specific configurations and overlays to enable the necessary GPIO controller for the `led0` alias.

The `CMakeLists.txt` for this test has a `project()` name that does not match the test's directory name (`gpio_basic_api` instead of `gpio_get_direction`). This is likely a copy-paste error from another test. The Zephyr build system may use the project name to correctly apply board-specific overlays and configurations for the test. A mismatch can lead to these configurations not being applied, resulting in the GPIO controller node being disabled and its driver not being built, which in turn causes the linker error.

The fix is to correct the project name in `tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction/CMakeLists.txt` to match the directory name. Additionally, the non-standard `FILE(GLOB ...)` will be replaced with the more conventional `target_sources()`.

tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction/CMakeLists.txt
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
project(gpio_basic_api)

FILE(GLOB app_sources src/*.c)
target_sources(app PRIVATE ${app_sources})
========
project(gpio_get_direction)

target_sources(app PRIVATE src/main.c)
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
